feasibilityFindings.classification: ARITHMETIC PROPERTIES OF FROZEN NUMBERS, SURFACED BY ACQUISITION PLANNING. This plan changes no methodology byte and proposes no amendment.

finding1.statement: SD4 caps SET_R at 4 pages per organisation per split; a gated split holds 45 organisations; the maximum attainable SET_R is therefore 180. SD5's shortfall rule extends SET_R 'never by relaxing the per-organisation cap', so extension cannot lift it either. The perGatedSplitContract.SET_R value of 200 is unreachable under the frozen caps.
finding1.bindingRequirementUnaffected: G2 and G4 have denominator 100 and SET_R_goldUnitPages_minimum is 100, both attainable within 180. The unreachable figure is a sample-size target, not a gate denominator.
finding1.recommendedReading: A realised SET_R of at most 180 violates no minimum and no maximum and is therefore CONFORMANT, consistent with R3's own rule that a corpus meeting every minimum and violating no maximum is conformant whatever its document count.
finding1.ownerConfirmationSought: whether a realised SET_R <= 180 is recorded as CONFORMANT (recommended) or as a freeze-blocking shortfall

finding2.statement: With SET_R at most 180 and at least 100 gold UNIT_PAGE required, SET_R must realise a gold UNIT_PAGE share of at least 55.6%. R3's carried planning assumption for gold UNIT_PAGE prevalence in a production-like sample is 0.175, so the required enrichment factor is at least 3.17x. The Track A/B ruleset's realised enrichment factor has never been measured.
finding2.risk: If enrichment falls short, SD5's extension is capped at 180 and the outcome is CORPUS_FREEZE_REFUSED after the full acquisition and labelling spend - the most expensive possible point of discovery.
finding2.mitigation: The enrichment factor is computable from DEV_TRAIN alone, which is unsealed and labelled first. Sequencing DEV_TRAIN labelling ahead of the gated splits is an operational choice inside the frozen methodology, not a change to it.

sealedDataDesign.principle: DEV_CONFIRM and FINAL_HOLDOUT labels MUST live in split-scoped files. The historical mixed 72-record and 160-record files are why the R3 section B boundary event was possible at all.
sealedDataDesign.threeSeparateRootsNotThreeSubdirectories: the cheapest real accident is a tool pointed one directory too high
failClosedMechanisms: separate filesystem roots, unreachable from one another by relative traversal
a split token on every sealed record; every reader is constructed with the split it may read and throws on the first differing token, before returning any row
a scoped reader with no default and no 'load the corpus' entry point
a CI firewall test asserting no committed file carries a gold label, item id or document hash for a gated split
sealedDataDesign.finalHoldoutIsSealedMoreStrictly: its sealed root is read by no tooling that exists at corpus-freeze time; the scoring runner capable of reading it is built after the freeze, under the separate HOLDOUT authorisation, and the freeze is what it is checked against

dualReviewResolution.problem: R3 section I defines dual-review scope in terms of GOLD (all gold UNIT_PAGE items, plus a 15% sample of gold negatives), but gold is the OUTPUT of dual review. Membership is defined by a value that does not exist until the set has been reviewed.
dualReviewResolution.howThatWasEstablished: Every scalar path in R3 was enumerated. Outside sectionI there are exactly five dual-review references (sectionD.expectedBurden.humanLabel, sectionH...requirements[2], sectionJ.splits[1].dualReviewRequired, sectionJ.splits[2].dualReviewRequired, revises.whatR3DoesNotChange[6]) plus openUnknowns[12]. None states how eligibility is determined before gold exists.
whyTheObviousImplementationIsInadmissibl: If reviewer A's label alone decides whether B sees an item, A's false positives are caught at 100% while A's false negatives escape at 85%. The correction is one-directional, so gold systematically under-counts UNIT_PAGE - and G2 and G4 are estimated on exactly that class.
Agreement computed over a set whose membership was decided by one rater's own outcome is conditional on that outcome, so the reported kappa would not measure what R3 commissioned it to measure.

C1.name: PRE_COMMITTED_POOL
C1.rule: DUAL_REVIEW_POOL = SET_R union (15% salted-rank sample of SET_P), fixed before any human sees any item

C2.name: SYMMETRIC_UNION_TRIGGER_WITH_FROZEN_PROBE
rules: FROZEN PROBE committed before labelling: items whose sha256("DUAL_REVIEW_V2_R2:" + goldId) falls in the lowest 15%

SYMMETRIC FIRST PASS: every item receives exactly one first label; which reviewer is first is decided by the frozen salted rank sha256("FIRST_REVIEWER_V2_GEN1:" + goldId), not by making A the reviewer of record
UNION TRIGGER: an item receives a second, blind, independent label iff it is in PROBE OR its first label is UNIT_PAGE OR its first label is NEEDS_REVIEW
C2.proof: An item can only become gold UNIT_PAGE if at least one human proposed UNIT_PAGE. Any item whose first label is UNIT_PAGE is dual-reviewed by the trigger; any item whose first label is not UNIT_PAGE can acquire that verdict only through a second label, which exists only if it was already dual-reviewed. Therefore {gold UNIT_PAGE} is a subset of {dual-reviewed}, with no forward reference to gold.
C2.residualLimitation: A first-pass false negative outside PROBE is never corrected. No design short of labelling 100% twice corrects it.
C2.residualIsMeasurableNotAssumedAway: PROBE is a frozen, label-independent, unbiased 15% sample, so the false-negative rate of first-pass negatives is estimable from it with an exact binomial interval using the same acceptanceStatistics.ts helper the gates use.
reportingDiscipline: the headline kappa is the PROBE-stratum kappa, the only stratum whose membership is label-independent
trigger-stratum agreement is reported separately and explicitly labelled conditional-on-first-label, never pooled into the headline figure
the estimated first-pass false-negative rate and its interval are committed to the corpus manifest as a stated limitation

C3.name: FULL_DUAL_REVIEW_OF_EVERY_ITEM
C3.whyNotRecommended: roughly 3x R3's planned human budget, which R3 explicitly sized and justified
